# nonNull

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** `null`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNull() — Checks whether a value is **not** `null`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonNull<T>(value: T | null): value is T;
```

`nonNull(value)` is the same test as `!isNull(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Strictly `null`. `undefined` is a separate case — `isNil` covers both.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type        | Description         |
| :-------- | :---------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| null` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not `null`; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonNull(undefined); // => true
nonNull(0); // => true
nonNull(""); // => true
nonNull(null); // => false
```
